sections.title: What is React?
sections.content:
# What is React? React is a **JavaScript library** for building user interfaces. It was developed by Facebook and is now maintained by Meta and the open-source community. ## Key Features - **Component-Based**: Build encapsulated components that manage their own state - **Declarative**: React makes it painless to create interactive UIs - **Learn Once, Write Anywhere**: You can develop new features without rewriting existing code ## Why Use React? 1. **Virtual DOM**: React uses a virtual DOM to improve performance 2. **Reusable Components**: Write once, use everywhere 3. **Strong Community**: Large ecosystem and community support ```jsx function Welcome(props) { return

Hello, {props.name}!

; } ``` This simple example shows how React components work with JSX syntax.

sections.title: Setting Up Your Environment
sections.content:
# Setting Up Your Development Environment

Before we start building React applications, we need to set up our development environment.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js** (version 14 or higher)
- **npm** or **yarn** package manager
- A code editor (VS Code recommended)

## Creating a New React App

The easiest way to get started is with Create React App:

```bash
npx create-react-app my-app
cd my-app
npm start
```

## Project Structure

After creating your app, you'll see this structure:

```
my-app/
  README.md
  node_modules/
  package.json
  public/
    index.html
    favicon.ico
  src/
    App.css
    App.js
    App.test.js
    index.css
    index.js
```

## Development Tools

- **React Developer Tools**: Browser extension for debugging
- **ESLint**: Code linting
- **Prettier**: Code formatting
